Troubleshooting Reproducibility: Tolerances, .Rprofile Traps, and Cross-Architecture Builds

Source: vignettes/troubleshooting-reproducibility.Rmd
troubleshooting-reproducibility.Rmd

Overview

Even well-intentioned R projects fail to reproduce in subtle real-world ways. This guide covers the four most common failure modes—and how rcapsule detects and resolves each one:

  1. Hidden .Rprofile portability hazards (machine-specific .libPaths(), setwd(), or hardcoded API keys).
  2. Apple Silicon (linux/arm64) vs. HPC/Cloud (linux/amd64) architecture mismatches and slow source-package builds.
  3. Monte Carlo and BLAS floating-point drift requiring explicit per-file numeric tolerances (atol/rtol).
  4. Non-deterministic binary/plot metadata (embedded timestamps in PNG/PDF graphics) and unexpected extra artifacts.

1. Catching .Rprofile Portability Traps and targets / here Projects

Local .Rprofile files often silently break containers when copied to another machine. scan_project() inspects .Rprofile (ignoring benign source("renv/activate.R") lines) and surfaces concrete hazards alongside targets pipelines, here::here() markers, zero-byte files, and unusual filenames:

library(rcapsule)

proj <- tempfile("rcapsule_troubleshoot_")
dir.create(file.path(proj, "data"), recursive = TRUE)

writeLines(
  c(
    "source('renv/activate.R')",
    ".libPaths('/Users/alex/R/custom-lib')",
    "setwd('/Users/alex/Desktop/my-paper')",
    "Sys.setenv(GITHUB_TOKEN = 'ghp_do_not_commit_me')"
  ),
  file.path(proj, ".Rprofile")
)

writeLines(
  c(
    "library(targets)",
    "library(here)",
    "list(tar_target(clean, read.csv(here::here('data', 'survey wave 1.csv'))))"
  ),
  file.path(proj, "_targets.R")
)
writeLines("", file.path(proj, ".here"))
write.csv(data.frame(id = 1:3, y = c(1, 2, 3)),
          file.path(proj, "data", "survey wave 1.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

sc <- scan_project(proj)
sc$rprofile_hazards
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>    line hazard               severity message                                   
#>   <int> <chr>                <chr>    <chr>                                     
#> 1     2 custom_libpaths      warning  .Rprofile modifies .libPaths(); hardcoded…
#> 2     2 hardcoded_local_path warning  .Rprofile references a machine-specific a…
#> 3     3 setwd_call           error    .Rprofile calls setwd(); use relative pat…
#> 4     3 hardcoded_local_path warning  .Rprofile references a machine-specific a…
#> 5     4 secret_in_rprofile   error    .Rprofile sets an apparent secret/token v…
sc$has_targets
#> [1] TRUE
sc$uses_here
#> [1] TRUE
sc$unusual_filenames
#> [1] "data/survey wave 1.csv"

When _targets.R is detected as the entrypoint, compile_dockerfile() and compile_apptainer() automatically emit targets::tar_make() as the container command:

df_tar <- compile_dockerfile(sc, r_version = "4.4.1")
tail(df_tar$lines, 5)
#> [1] "COPY --chown=capsule:capsule . /capsule/"                                 
#> [2] "USER capsule"                                                             
#> [3] "HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \\"
#> [4] "    CMD Rscript -e \"quit(status = 0)\" || exit 1"                        
#> [5] "CMD [\"Rscript\", \"-e\", \"targets::tar_make()\"]"

2. Apple Silicon (arm64) vs. HPC (amd64) & Posit PPM Binaries

Developers on Apple Silicon laptops (arm64) frequently deploy containers to x86_64 cloud hosts or university HPC clusters (amd64). scan_project() records host architecture hints in scan$architecture, and both compile_dockerfile() and compile_compose() support explicit platform pinning plus Posit Package Manager (use_ppm = TRUE) binary repositories:

sc$architecture
#> $host_arch
#> [1] "amd64"
#> 
#> $host_platform
#> [1] "x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
#> 
#> $is_apple_silicon
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $recommended_container_platform
#> [1] "linux/amd64"
#> 
#> $hpc_target_platform
#> [1] "linux/amd64"
#> 
#> $notes
#> character(0)

df_amd64 <- compile_dockerfile(
  sc,
  r_version  = "4.4.1",
  platform   = "linux/amd64",
  use_ppm    = TRUE,
  ppm_distro = "jammy",
  ppm_date   = "2026-01-15"
)

grep("^(FROM|    R_REPOS=)", df_amd64$lines, value = TRUE)
#> [1] "FROM --platform=linux/amd64 rocker/r-ver:4.4.1 AS builder"                  
#> [2] "    R_REPOS=https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/jammy/2026-01-15"
#> [3] "FROM --platform=linux/amd64 rocker/r-ver:4.4.1 AS runtime"

Passing use_ppm = FALSE switches back to source package snapshots when compiling against custom system libraries or niche architectures.

3. Configuring Exact vs. Per-File Monte Carlo Tolerances

Deterministic summary tables should verify bit-for-bit (atol = 0, rtol = 0), while MCMC posterior summaries or cross-BLAS matrix decompositions may warrant explicit numeric tolerances. compare_artifacts() and create_capsule_manifest() support nested JSON, RDS (including matrices, data frames, and NA/NaN/Inf alignment), CSV, and TSV tolerances via atol/rtol (or abs_tol/rel_tol):

f_ref <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
f_run <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")

baseline <- list(
  posterior_mean = c(alpha = 1.2500, beta = -0.4000),
  cov_matrix = matrix(c(0.04, 0.01, 0.01, 0.09), nrow = 2),
  diagnostics = list(rhat = c(1.001, 1.002), divergent = 0L)
)
reproduced <- baseline
reproduced$posterior_mean <- c(alpha = 1.2503, beta = -0.3998)
reproduced$cov_matrix[1, 2] <- 0.0102

saveRDS(baseline, f_ref)
saveRDS(reproduced, f_run)

# Strict zero tolerance fails on SHA-256 mismatch
compare_artifacts(f_ref, f_run, atol = 0, rtol = 0)$status
#> [1] "mismatch"

# Explicit Monte Carlo tolerance passes and reports exact max observed error
res_mc <- compare_artifacts(f_ref, f_run, atol = 1e-3, rtol = 1e-3)
res_mc[c("status", "passed", "max_abs_diff", "max_rel_diff", "details")]
#> $status
#> [1] "within_tolerance"
#> 
#> $passed
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $max_abs_diff
#> [1] 3e-04
#> 
#> $max_rel_diff
#> [1] 0.01960784
#> 
#> $details
#> [1] "Verified within tolerance (max_abs_diff=3e-04, max_rel_diff=0.01961)."

4. Handling Non-Deterministic Plot Metadata & Extra Artifacts

Binary PDF and PNG files often embed creation timestamps or graphics-engine metadata that change SHA-256 digests across OS versions even when the plotted data are identical. Best practice in rcapsule:

  1. Always save the underlying numerical data table (results/fig1_data.csv or .rds) alongside the rendered figure and register the numerical table in outputs with exact or tolerance bounds.
  2. Use strict_outputs = TRUE in verify_capsule() during CI gating to catch scripts that unexpectedly drop temporary files or log artifacts into the workspace.
  3. Keep ambient host secrets safe: verify_capsule(..., scrub_secrets = TRUE) automatically strips AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, and other credential variables before executing the isolated sandbox.
